body:
`help work` printed nearly the whole help, though the reference says `help <command>` lists that command's options.

**Cause** (`main.rs::agent_help`): a topic first matches paragraphs that have an indented line (`  `) starting with the command. `work` (`Work records, kept between sessions: work add …`) and the `Project: build | format | run <name>` line are not indented, so nothing matches. It then falls back to **every paragraph that has the word anywhere**. A common word like `work`, `run`, `build` or `format` appears in most of the reference, so the agent gets almost all of it.

**Fix**
- In `reference.txt`'s *Commands in full*, give every command its own indented entry (`work add`, `work list`, `work done <id>`, `build`, `build plan`, `format`, `run <name>`), the way the other commands are written. Then `help <command>` finds each one by its entry.
- `help <command>` answers with the paragraph that holds the command's entry, not every paragraph that mentions the word. Drop the fallback that matches any word. A command with no entry gets `No command <x>` and the list of command names, not the whole reference.
- Strategy runs and task runs keep their own reduced sets, as they do now.

**Tests**
- For every command in the summary table (the `Commands (…)` block), `agent_help(cmd)` contains that command's entry and is much shorter than the full help.
- `help work` and `help run` each return their own section.
- `help nosuch` returns the list of names, not the reference.
- Extend the reference layout check (`solace-cli/tests/reference_layout.py`, D-143) so it fails when a command in the summary table has no indented entry in *Commands in full*.
title: help: one command's section only
